newsitem.title: GERMANY: German finance ministry denies budget cuts report.
newsitem.headline: German finance ministry denies budget cuts report.

text.p: The German finance ministry on Tuesday denied a newspaper report that it had imposed a 15 percent spending cut on government departments as of May 1.
Referring to a government circular obtained by the Berliner Morgenpost newspaper, a ministry spokesman said that the 15

The ministry said certain government grants had in December been placed under a temporary freeze, and that 85 percent of the funds had been released in April. The remaining 15 percent was being kept for possible savings, the spokesman said.

The German government is under pressure to reduce spending and raise revenue as it scrambles to meet the three percent deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) goal for Europe's monetary union, due to start in 1999.
Finance minister Theo Waigel has already said that he is retaining the right to impose a government spending freeze depending on the results of a key estimate of tax receipts due Thursday.

The May tax estimates for 1997 are due on Thursday. With analysts predicting that a shortfall of as much as 20 billion marks may be announced, Waigel may have to take what some say must be drastic steps to cut spending.
The government has said it expects a shortfall of around eight billion marks.
